questions.stem: At schematic design, an owner wants a cost estimate organized by building systems (foundations, shell, interiors, services) so it can compare design alternatives. Which classification system is most appropriate?

options.explanation: Correct. UniFormat organizes cost by building elements and systems, which suits early estimates and comparing alternatives.
MasterFormat organizes by work results and trades. It's better for detailed estimates once specifications exist.
UDS organizes drawing sets, not cost estimates.
LOD describes how reliable model elements are. It isn't a cost classification.

questions.explanation: Early, system-level comparison → UniFormat. Specification-level detail → MasterFormat.

questions.stem: Under the Uniform Drawing System, what does sheet number A-301 most likely represent?

options.explanation: Correct. A = architectural discipline; 3 = sections sheet type; 01 = sequence number.
Plans use sheet type 1 (e.g., A-103 for the third plan sheet).
Details use sheet type 5 (e.g., A-501).

options.text: An architectural site plan for building 3
options.explanation: UDS sheet numbers encode discipline, sheet type and sequence, not building numbers.

questions.explanation: UDS: discipline letter + sheet-type digit + sequence (0 general, 1 plans, 2 elevations, 3 sections, 4 large-scale, 5 details, 6 schedules).

questions.stem: A firm with frequent coordination errors between architectural and MEP documents wants firm-wide process improvements. Which measures are most effective?

options.text: Adopt a BIM execution plan defining model responsibilities, exchange schedule and LOD by milestone
options.explanation: Correct. Clear modeling responsibilities and exchange timing reduce coordination gaps.

options.text: Hold scheduled clash-detection and coordination reviews before major issues
options.explanation: Correct. Routine clash detection catches conflicts before documents are issued.

options.text: Use milestone QC checklists, with an independent reviewer before permit and bid sets
options.explanation: Correct. Structured QC by a fresh reviewer finds errors the team misses.

options.text: Eliminate consultant meetings to save fee
options.explanation: Less coordination increases errors.

options.text: Let each consultant use its own sheet numbering and layer standards
options.explanation: Inconsistent standards make coordination and review harder.

options.text: Delay all coordination until construction RFIs reveal the conflicts
options.explanation: Finding conflicts in the field is the most expensive way to coordinate.

questions.explanation: Coordination quality = defined responsibilities + scheduled exchanges + systematic QC.

questions.stem: A historic warehouse will be converted into apartments. The owner wants to keep its character-defining features while adding modern systems and new interior layouts. Which Secretary of the Interior's treatment fits best?

options.explanation: Correct. Rehabilitation allows compatible alterations and additions for a new use while preserving historic character.
Restoration returns a property to its appearance at a particular period and removes later features. It's not suited to a new use.
Reconstruction recreates a vanished building with new construction.
Preservation focuses on maintaining and repairing existing fabric with minimal change, which isn't enough for a conversion.

questions.stem: In a CSI three-part specification section, where are installation requirements and field quality control found?

options.explanation: Correct. Part 3 covers examination, preparation, installation, field quality control, cleaning and protection.
Part 1 covers administrative requirements: submittals, quality assurance, delivery, warranty.
Part 2 covers manufacturers, materials, products and fabrication.
Division 01 has project-wide General Requirements, not section-specific installation.

questions.explanation: Part 1 General · Part 2 Products · Part 3 Execution.

questions.stem: A contractor needs model elements accurate enough for fabrication and installation. Which level of development is required?

options.explanation: Correct. LOD 400 includes the detail needed for fabrication, assembly and installation.
LOD 200 is approximate geometry, enough for design studies.
LOD 300 is precise design geometry, but it isn't fabrication-level detail.
LOD 100 is conceptual.

questions.explanation: LOD 100 conceptual · 200 approximate · 300 precise · 350 interfaces · 400 fabrication · 500 as-built.

questions.stem: A firm is preparing its first project in an occupied hospital. Which process adjustments are most important?

options.text: Develop detailed construction phasing and infection-control requirements with the facility
options.explanation: Correct. Work in occupied healthcare facilities must protect patients and operations.

options.text: Coordinate early with the healthcare regulatory agencies and applicable healthcare design guidelines
options.explanation: Correct. Healthcare projects face more regulatory review than typical commercial work.

options.text: Use the firm's standard office-building details without review
options.explanation: Healthcare has specific requirements that standard commercial details may not meet.

options.text: Skip existing-conditions verification to save time
options.explanation: Occupied renovations need careful verification of existing conditions.

options.text: Rely solely on the contractor to plan phasing
options.explanation: Phasing affects the design documents and operations. The architect must help plan it.

options.text: Issue a single bid package with no phasing to simplify bidding
options.explanation: Occupied hospitals usually need phased work to keep operating.

questions.explanation: Project type changes the process: healthcare means regulatory coordination, phasing and infection control.

questions.stem: Which specification method states required results and leaves the means of achieving them to the contractor?

options.explanation: Correct. Performance specs define required outcomes and test criteria.
Descriptive specs detail materials and installation rather than results.
Closed proprietary specs name specific products with no substitutions.
Reference standard specs rely on cited industry standards, not stated outcomes.

questions.explanation: Performance = what it must do. Prescriptive = what it is and how to install it.

questions.stem: A firm wants a record-retention policy that best protects it against late claims. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Keep key project records at least through the applicable statute of repose and contractual claim periods
options.explanation: Correct. Records are critical defense evidence. Keep them as long as claims can be brought.

options.text: Discard project records one year after substantial completion
options.explanation: Claims can arrive many years later. Early disposal leaves the firm unable to defend itself.

options.text: Keep only the final drawings and discard correspondence
options.explanation: Correspondence, meeting minutes and field reports are often the most important defense records.

options.text: Give all records to the owner at closeout
options.explanation: The firm needs its own records. Owners receive specified deliverables, not the firm's files.

questions.explanation: Retention policy should match the claims exposure period (repose + contract limits).

questions.stem: A retail client builds 30 stores a year from a prototype. Which practice-wide resource most improves efficiency and consistency?

options.text: A maintained prototype standards package with version control and a site-adaptation checklist
options.explanation: Correct. Controlled prototype documents and a site-adaptation process give consistency across many stores.

options.text: A custom design for each store to show creativity
options.explanation: Custom design for each store defeats the purpose of a prototype program.

options.text: Copying the last store's drawings without checking the local code
options.explanation: Each site has its own code, zoning and site conditions that must be reviewed.

options.text: Letting each project team keep its own version of the prototype
options.explanation: Multiple uncontrolled versions lead to errors and inconsistency.

questions.explanation: Repetitive programs → controlled standards + site-adaptation procedures.
